subject: Authorization audit: service-connector role mapping & shadow-account trace
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@medsync.io>, security@medsync.io
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Authorization audit: service-connector role mapping & shadow-account trace

Hi Alex / MedSync security team —

As part of the SIG/SOC2 evidence pack we discussed, we need a scoped deliverable focused on service connectors and the service-account/service-connector roles that interact with our integration. The auditor asked for a concise bundle covering: 

- SCIM delta export for the tenant covering 2027-05-01 through 2027-05-27 (created/deactivated/role assignments)
- Role mapping CSV showing which connector/service accounts are permitted to perform admin or delegated-admin actions (include role IDs and human-friendly names)
- Session snapshots or JIT logs for the service-connector tokens around any elevated role activations during that window

Can you confirm which of the above you can provide and when? Auditor timeline: evidence must be uploaded by EOD Monday 2027-05-31. If you have a preferred export format, we can accept CSV/JSON/structured logs — we will handle redaction.

A couple of clarifying points the auditor highlighted: 
- If you have any legacy "connector-admin" roles that were historically granted to service accounts, please annotate where those overlap with modern RBAC roles.
- If SCIM provisioning uses delta syncs but the values have been normalized (e.g., role IDs changed), include a mapping table or note so we can reconcile hashes.

Please attach the exports to this thread (or share via the Drive link below) and ping me here. If you can’t meet the Monday window, suggest the earliest time you can deliver and we’ll notify the auditors.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan Blake
Principal, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments requested: role_mapping, scim_delta, session_snapshot

From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@medsync.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medsync.io, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Authorization audit: service-connector role mapping & shadow-account trace

Thanks Jordan — good to sync on this. Short answer: we can provide everything on your list, with the following caveats and timeline: 

- SCIM delta export: we can produce a delta JSON export (audit-friendly) for 2027-05-01 to 2027-05-27 by EOD Monday (2027-05-31). It will include user/entitlement events and role assignment changes.
- Role mapping CSV: available today, I’ll attach a cleaned CSV with role_id, role_name, allowed_actions, assigned_service_accounts. We will redact any PII.
- Session snapshots / JIT activation logs: our platform retains token/session traces for 30 days; we can pull the snapshots for the specific connectors if you can provide the connector IDs or service-account emails. We can also provide a short explanation of how delegated-admin is represented in our logs.

Question: when you say "service-connector tokens around elevated role activations," do you want every token issuance event for connectors that held an elevated role, or only events where an elevation workflow was triggered (i.e., ephemeral elevation)?

I’ll attach the role mapping CSV in my next email. If you prefer, we can drop the exports to the shared Drive: https://drive.medsync.io/redwood-evidence (we can also SFTP if you need an air-gapped handoff).

—Alex
Senior Security Engineer, MedSync Health

Attachment: role_mapping_20270528.csv (upcoming)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@medsync.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Authorization audit: service-connector role mapping & shadow-account trace

Alex — quick internal note and a couple requests from our side: 

1) Connector IDs: we’ll take the full set, but please prioritize connectors that have the connector scope "write:users" or "admin:provisioning" — those are the ones auditors flag as higher risk.

2) Shadow accounts / orphaned service accounts: please include any service accounts that have not had activity in the last 90 days but still hold privileged roles. If you can tag them with last_seen timestamp, that will speed the attestation.

3) If SCIM deltas include transformed role IDs, include the mapping file you mentioned. Marcus — can you prepare a quick RBAC crosswalk template I can drop into Alex’s CSV? I’ll attach after lunch.

I’ve created a temporary Drive folder and set share-to-view for MedSync security: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/MedSync/SCIM-deltas-20270528 — please upload there if easier.

Thanks,
Soojin
Security Integrations Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@medsync.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@medsync.io>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Authorization audit: service-connector role mapping & shadow-account trace

All — attaching the cleaned role mapping CSV and a compressed SCIM delta export for the requested window.

We included: role_mapping_20270528.csv (columns: role_id, role_name, allowed_actions, assigned_service_accounts, last_seen), scim_delta_20270501-20270527.json (events array with timestamps), session_snapshot_20270527.log (token issuance and activation events filtered for connectors flagged by Soojin).

To Soojin’s question: we included both token issuance events and explicit elevation actions (the file flags elevated sessions with "elevation=true"). If auditors want only one type, tell us and we’ll filter.

We’ll keep the Drive folder live for 7 days; please confirm when you’ve downloaded and if any additional redaction or mapping is required.

Regards,
Alex
Senior Security Engineer, MedSync Health

Attachments: role_mapping_20270528.csv, scim_delta_20270501-20270527.json, session_snapshot_20270527.log
